title: Hoglet — 3yo African pygmy hedgehog: drooling with a mouth mass
presentation: 3-year-old female African pygmy hedgehog, drooling for three weeks, dropping food, and the owner has noticed a red mass at the front of her mouth. She has lost 90 g.

stages.title: Assess the patient
stages.briefing: Weight 320 g, down from 410 g. Under anaesthesia: a 9 mm friable, ulcerated red mass arising from the gingiva at the left mandibular incisor-canine region, bleeding on contact. Two adjacent teeth mobile. Halitosis. Mandibular lymph node not clearly enlarged. No wobbling, normal gait, no ataxia.
stages.prompt: Which findings shape the differential list?

options.label: A friable ulcerated gingival mass with adjacent tooth mobility
options.detail: Invasive local disease rather than simple gingivitis

options.label: 90 g weight loss with dropping of food
options.detail: Functional impact of oral pain

options.label: Age three years in this species
options.detail: The age at which hedgehog neoplasia becomes common

options.label: Halitosis
options.detail: Present with any oral lesion

options.label: Normal gait with no ataxia
options.detail: Useful — it argues against wobbly hedgehog syndrome — but a negative

stages.explanation: Oral masses in middle-aged African pygmy hedgehogs are usually neoplastic rather than inflammatory, and tooth mobility beside a friable mass suggests bone invasion. This species is famously tumour-prone from around three years old, which is why the age is a real piece of clinical evidence and not just a demographic detail.

stages.title: Choose the tests
stages.briefing: She is already anaesthetised, which is the moment to gather everything.

options.label: Incisional biopsy of the mass for histopathology
options.detail: The only way to name the tumour

options.label: Skull radiographs or CT of the mandible
options.detail: Bone lysis and surgical margins

options.label: Fine needle aspirate cytology of the mandibular lymph node
options.detail: Regional metastasis

options.label: Thoracic radiographs
options.detail: Distant metastasis before committing to surgery

options.label: Haematology and biochemistry
options.detail: Anaesthetic and treatment fitness in a 320 g patient

options.label: Bacterial culture of the mass as the definitive test
options.detail: It will grow oral flora and answer nothing

options.label: Empirical antibiotics and review in three weeks with no biopsy
options.detail: Delays diagnosis of an aggressive tumour

stages.explanation: Anaesthesia in a 320 g hedgehog is the scarce resource, so everything gets done in one episode: biopsy, imaging of the jaw and chest, node aspirate and bloods. Culturing an oral mass is the classic wasted test — it grows mouth flora whatever the lesion is. Treating empirically and reviewing later is how these tumours become inoperable.

stages.title: Interpret the results
stages.briefing: Histopathology: squamous cell carcinoma with invasion of the underlying bone, incomplete margins on the incisional sample. CT: osteolysis of the left rostral mandible around the mobile teeth, no mandibular fracture. Lymph node cytology: reactive hyperplasia, no neoplastic cells. Thoracic radiographs: no pulmonary nodules. Haematology: mild anaemia. Biochemistry: albumin 24 g/L (low), urea and creatinine normal, ALT normal.
stages.prompt: Which conclusions do these results support?

options.label: Oral squamous cell carcinoma with local bone invasion
options.detail: Histology plus osteolysis on CT

options.label: No detectable regional or pulmonary metastasis at this point
options.detail: Reactive node and clear thoracic radiographs

options.label: Nutritional support is needed before and after any surgery
options.detail: Albumin 24 g/L after 90 g of weight loss

options.label: Antibiotics alone will not control this lesion
options.detail: It is neoplastic, not primarily infectious

options.label: Wobbly hedgehog syndrome is a concurrent diagnosis
options.detail: No neurological signs and nothing here supports it

options.label: The absence of nodules on radiographs excludes metastasis
options.detail: Radiographs miss small metastases; it is undetected rather than absent

stages.explanation: Naming the tumour and its bone invasion is what makes the surgical conversation honest: mandibulectomy in a 320 g animal is possible but demanding, and incomplete margins on the biopsy predict how hard clean margins will be. The distinction between "no metastasis detected" and "no metastasis" is not pedantry — it is what stops an owner being promised a cure.

stages.title: Commit to a diagnosis
stages.briefing: Squamous cell carcinoma on histopathology with rostral mandibular osteolysis, reactive node, clear thoracic radiographs, albumin 24 g/L, 90 g weight loss.

options.label: Oral squamous cell carcinoma with mandibular bone invasion, no metastasis detected
options.detail: The tumour, its local extent and the honest staging

options.label: Chronic ulcerative gingivostomatitis
options.detail: Histology shows carcinoma

options.label: Dental abscess with osteomyelitis
options.detail: The lysis is neoplastic invasion, confirmed on biopsy

options.label: Wobbly hedgehog syndrome
options.detail: A neurodegenerative disease with no oral lesion

options.label: Oral papilloma
options.detail: Benign and non-invasive, contradicted by the histology

stages.explanation: This diagnosis frames a decision rather than a prescription: partial mandibulectomy with analgesia and nutritional support, or palliation with analgesia and assisted feeding, discussed frankly with an owner whose hedgehog has an aggressive tumour and a low albumin. Staging it carefully is what lets that conversation be specific instead of hopeful.
